CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE
  REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY,  JANUARY  28, 2025

  AMENDED

CALL  TO ORDER  Maria  Davila,  Mayor  called  a Regular  City  Council  Meeting  to order at
  6:56 p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley,  Director  of Parks and Recreation

PLEDGEOFALLEGIANCE  WendyO'Kelly,DirectorofAdministrativeServices

ROLL  CALL  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor  Maria  Davila,  Vice Mayor  Joshua Barron,  Council  Member  Maria
  del Pilar Avalos,  Council  Member  Gil Hurtado  and Council  Member  Al
  Rios;  City Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City  Manager  Rob Houston,  City
  Attorney  Rail  F. Salinas

CERIIFICATES  Recognition  of Chief  Darren  Arakawa  as outgoing  President  of the Los
  Angeles  County  Police  Chiefs  Association  and Honoring  the incoming
  President,  Chief  Maru'iy  Cid.

2
COMMUNITY  DEV/

HOUSING  Following  the conclusion  of the Public  Hearing,  the City  Council
  unanimously  continued  items A & B to the next regularly  scheduled  City
  Council  meeting  of February  28, 2025,  by motion  of Council  Member
  Hurtado  and seconded  by Council  Member  Rios.:

  a.  Adopting  Resolution  approving  Substantial  Amendment  No. 7 to the
  Fiscal  Year 2019-2020  Annual  Action  Plan;  Substantial  Amendment
  No. 2 to the Fiscal  Year 2020-2021  Annual  Action  Plan;  Substantial
  Amendment  No. 4 to the Fiscal  Year 2022-2023  Annual  Action  Plan;
  Substantial  Amendment  No. 1 to Fiscal  Year 2023-2024  Aru'iual  Action
  Plan; and Substantial  Amendment  No.  I to Fiscal  Year 2024-2025
  Annual  Action  Plan programming  Community  Development  Block
  Grant  ("CDBG")  fiinds  to the Street Improvement  Project  and South
  Gate Park Improvement  (Attachment  A); and

  b.  Authorizing  the City  Manager  or the Community  Development
  Director  to initiate  appropriate  action  necessary  to implement  projects
  and programs  as noted  in the FY 2024-2025  Annual  Action  Plan.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council  Member  Avalos,  yes; Council  Member  Hurtado,
  yes; Council  Member  Rios,  yes; Vice  Mayor  Barron,  yes; Mayor  Davila,
  yes.

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  (NON-AGENDA

ITEMS)  Ernesto  Gomez,  Field  Representative  for Nanette  Barragan  - 44'h District  -

  Sharing  resources  for the community  regarding  the immigration  and
  deportation  issues  with  this  new  administration.

  Mayor,  Davila  - LAUSD  meeting  regarding  irnrnigration  on Thursday,
  January  30, 2025,  4:30pm  at Legacy  High  School.  A very  important
  meeting  regarding  your  rights.

  Council  Member,  Hurtado  - Spoke  about  an issue  he had years  ago with
  immigration.  To our community,  please  be vigilant.

  We need to be aware  of all the potential  cuts that  might  come  to our city
  and state.

  Council  Member,  Avalos  - Thanks  Mr.  Gomez  for attending  this meeting
  to inform  our community.

  Inform  Congresswoman  Barragan  that  she has full  support  of the City  of

  South  Gate.

  Ernesto  Gomez,  Field  Representative  for Nanette  Barragan  - 44"1 District  -

  Keep  us in mind  with  those  that  are arrested  and held.  We will  continue  to
  provide  information  as we receive  it. Information  will  be placed  on the

  city  website.

  Vice  Mayor,  Barron  - We stand  in solidarity  with  our residents,  and we
  will  not use the police  department  to enforce  any immigration  laws.

  Mario  Dominguez,  Resident  - Requesting  the splash  pad item  to be placed

  on the next  agenda  meeting.

  Jennifer  Daley,  Advocate  - Speaks  on behalf  of residents  who  have
  concerns  opposing  illegal  truck  yards  at 8530  Alameda  st., 4552 Ardine
  st., and 9313 Rayo Ave.  Asking  city  to uphold  the law  and enforce
  environmental  protections  and shut down  these  toxic  truck  yards.

  Joanne  Kim,  Cancer  Research  Advocate  - Expressing  concerns  and

  opposing  illegal  truck  yards,  particularly  the one near 8530 Alameda
  Street.  States  levels  of contamination  found  near  South  Gate  are a public
  health  crisis.

  Kirby  Blanton,  Works  in Early  Education  and Mental  Health  - Believes

  damage  is being  caused  by deals  between  City  Council  and truck  yards.
  Asking  the city  for transparency,  enforcing  environmental  protections,  and

  ensuring  money  meant  to serve  our community.

ITEMS)  CONT'D  Gabriela  Gutierrez,  Educator  - Speaks on behalf  of residents  who have
  concerns  opposing  illegal  truck  yards at 8530 Alameda  st., 4552 Ardine
  st., and 9313 Rayo Ave. Asking  city to uphold  the law and enforce
  environmental  protections  and shut down  these toxic  truck  yards.

  Roger  Satti, Volleyball  Coach  at Southeast  High  School  - Requesting
  sponsorship  from  council  and local business  for an opportunity  to compete
  in the Volleyball  Games  in Hawaii.  This sponsorship  will  cover travel,
  accommodations,  transportation  fees, and other essential  costs.

  Marisol  Carpinteiro,  Resident/Mother  - Requesting  support/funds  for
  students  to travel  to Hawaii  and compete  in the Volleyball  Tournament
  April  13-18,  2025.

  Lizette  Ruiz,  Resident  - Thank  you for providing  space to speak about the
  immigration  issues. Glad to see signs within  the community.

  Previously  we had isSues with  the park playgrounds  and equipment  at
  several  parks.  Recently,  I visited  some parks with  my minor  child  and was
  happy  to see many  improvements  made to the parks.  Very thankfiil.

  Amy  Lu, Leeland  R. Weaver  Librarian  - Currently  closed  for renovations.
  Effective  immediately,  Hollydale  Library  will  be open on an additional
  day, which  will  be Saturdays  from  10am-6pm.

  Introduction  of Stephanie  Lin overseeing  Hollydale  in the meantime.  The
  upcoming  programs  are Storytime  for ages 2-5-year-old.  Book  Club  for
  Adults  in English/Spanish.  Ceramic  Mugs,  etc.

  Omar  Ruiz,  Student/Resident  - Opposing  illegal  truck  yards at 8530
  Alarneda  st., 4552 Ardine  st., and 9313 Rayo Ave.

  Armando  Velasquez,  Resident/Kiwanis  Club - Aru'iouncement/Events:
  February  13, 2025, Valentine's  Bingo  Card. February  15, 2025,  Clean  Up
  Day. $7000  in scholarships  applications  will  be accepted  in a couple
  weeks.

  Javier,  Resident  - Upset  that nothing  is being  done regarding  the truck
  yard issue. Thank  you to Chief Arakawa  for not being  involved  in
  immigration  issues. Interesting  in knowing  how prepared  the city is for
  wildfires?

EMAIL:  Veronica  Figueroa,  Resident  - Ongoing  request  for a crosswalk  on Long
  Beach  Blvd  and Orchard  Place. Progress  is slow  and it is a remains  a
  safety  concern  for students/parents.

EMAIL  CONT'D  Claudia  Rivera,  Resident  - Reminder  that Council  Member  Al Rios is
  unable  to vote on the SoFive  project  when  the issue of alcohol  is
  discussed.  He has openly  been campaigning  against  it by meeting  with
  people  and sending  emails  about his opposition.

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS

  CITY  OFFICIALS  Arturo  Cervantes,  Director  of Public  Works  - Responds  to the request  for
FROM

  a crosswalk  on Orchard  Place.  KIPP  Elementary  School  did not choose
  this intersection  to be a safe intersection  for student  access. It is not safe
  for the city to install  a crosswalk  due to a traffic  signal  close by. It is
  currently  not safe to do so.

  Regarding  the recent  wildfire  preparedness  questions.  The city is prepared
  and has a reliable  water  system  and water reservoirs  with  over 14 million
  gallons  of water  storage  and interties  with  other  cities.

  Steve Costley,  Director  of Parks & Recreation  - Thursday,  January  30,
  2025,  is the Grand  Opening  for Hollydale  Park at 4pm.  The public  is
  welcome  to join  us. Residents  were notified  via door hangers  and social
  media.  12221  Industrial  Avenue  South  Gate.

  Wendy  O'Kelly,  Director  ofAdministrative  Services-Nothing  to report.

  Jon Hamilton,  Director  of Human  Resources  - Open positions  available
  within  the City  of South  Gate. Informing  the public  to go to our city
  website  and apply.

  Darren  Arakawa,  Police  Chief  - We are currently  working  on a report  but

  with  respect  to speeding,  in 2024 we issued 2300 violations.  Speeding  is
  county  wide issue. We are doing  our very  best.

  Rob Houston,  City  Manager  - Update  on progress  regarding  illegal  truck
  years. Mr. C's Towing is working with  the city regarding  zoning  permits.
  Some items we are unable to speak on this time.  Know  that we are
  currently  working  on these issues.

  Council  Member  Avalos  - Thank  you to Congresswoman  Barragan  and
  the community  that are present  at this council meeting.

  Council  Member,  Hurtado  - Frustrating  to see drivers  disregard  for public
  safety.  Drivers  are out of control.To those that are here regarding
  environmental  issues. You are not being ignored. We hear you and
  understand  this issue.

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS
FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS

CONT'D  Council  Member,  Rios - Thank  you to the resident  and public  present  at
  this meeting.  Understands  the concerns  of our residents.  Start day for the
  East Los Angeles  College  is February  10, 2025. There  are plenty  of classes
  available.

  Jaime Escalante  Math  Program  are available  at the college.  Gift  cards are
  still  available  for our city. Please support  small businesses.

  Vice Mayor,  Barron  - Thank  you to Wendy  O'Kelly  for your hard work
  and time at the city.

  Thank  you to Teddy's  Red Tacos for feeding  firefighters  and the
  community  affected  by the fires.

  South  Gate Junior  Athletics  Association  - February  8'h we have softball
  and baseball  sign-ups  9-12pm.

  Congratulations  to 7 student  athletes  who were chosen  by the City
  Sectional  CIF List - IS' Team All-League  representing  South  Gate
  Schools.

  Congratulations  to the Aztec  Cheerleaders  who also won  Ist & 2ndplace.

  Mayor,  Davila  - We must keep an eye on our seniors.  Will  be visiting  two
  schools  and would  like to inform  them about the immigration  issues.

  Thank  you to residents  and visitors  for being  here and speaking  on several
  issues. We have an open-door  policy  and welcome  anyone  at our city hall
  meetings.

CONSENT  CALENDAR  Agenda  Items  3, 4 and 5 were approved  by motion  of Council  Member
  Rios and seconded  by Mayor  Davila.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council  Member  Avalos,  yes; Council  Member  Hurtado,
  yes (recused  from  items  3 and 4); Council  Member  Rios, yes; Vice Mayor
  Barron,  yes; Mayor  Davila,  yes.

LANDSCAPING  The City  Council  adopted  Resolution  No. 2025-05-CC  entitled  Resolution
  of the City  Council  of the City  of South  Gate, California,  authorizing  the
  application  for the Statewide  Park Development  and Community
  Revitalization  Program  Grant  Funds  (Proposition  1 Lower  Los Angeles
  River  Program  Grant  Funds)  requesting  $1,100,342  in grants to :tund
  construction  of the Urban  Orchard,  City  Project  No. 539-PRK,  and
  authorizing  the City  Manager,  or his designee,  to execute,  on behalf  of the
  City  of South  Gate ("City"),  all documents  required  to submit  the
  application  and implement  the grant during  Consent  Calendar.

LANDSCAPING  The City  Council  approved  items A & B during  consent  calendar:

  a.  Amendment  No. 5 to Contract  No. 2021-147-CC  with  BKF  Engineers,
  Inc., (Agreement)  for additional  design  and construction  support
  services  necessary  to prepare  design  and construction  documents  to
  repair  Industrial  Avenue  as a part of the Citywide  Residential
  Resurfacing  Project,  Phase IV, City  Project  No. 699-ST,  in an amount
  not-to-exceed  $6,226;  and

  b.  Authorized  the Mayor  to execute  Amendment  No.  5 to Contract  No.
  2021-147-CC  in a form  acceptable  to the City Attorney.

MINUTES  The City  Council  unanimously  approved  items A, B & C during  consent
  calendar:

  a.  Special  and Regular  Meeting  minutes  of November  12, 2024;

  b.  Special  and Regular  Meeting  minutes  of November  26, 2024;  and

  c.  SpecialandRegularMeetingminutesofDecemberlO,2024.

LAND  USE PLANNING

ADMIN  The City  Council  approved  items A, B & C by motion  of Council  Member
  Hurtado  and seconded  by Vice Mayor  Barron:

  a.  Discussing  an ordinance  amendment  regarding  industrial  uses; land
  use improvements  surrounding  two future  transit  centers;  and
  enhancements  to commercial  corridors  to encourage  new businesses
  and development;

  b.  Providing  direction  to staff on releasing  a request  for proposal  ("RFP")
  to obtain  a planning  and environmental  consultant  qualified  in
  addressing  the items above,  including  preparing  an environmental
  document;  and

  c.  Directing  staff to release the RFP to qualified  consultants  to solicit
  planning  and environmental  services.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council  Member  Avalos,  yes; Council  Member  Hurtado,
  yes; Council  Member  Rios, no; Vice Mayor  Barron,  yes; Mayor  Davila,
  yes.
